_comment: Copy to sources.json to give the overlay numbers. Three ways to fill it: (1) the community feed below, built only from games players chose to share, free and never paywalled; (2) your own games, via `collect.py` then `collect.py --local-feed`, which writes this file for you pointing at data/feed; (3) any source you have the right to use. {time} = all-time | past-seven | past-three | last-patch, {mmr} = 100|50|25|10|1. A value may be an https URL or a local file path. Delete a line to leave that table empty; the tool shows 'no numbers' rather than failing. The community feed is brand new, so expect thin samples, flagged as thin, until it fills up. Share your own games with: collect.py --upload http://165.227.41.29
_comment_mmr: {mmr} is your --mmr bracket. A feed publishes a bracket only once it holds enough games, so top-1% may not exist yet; when it doesn't, the tool falls back to the all-players file and says on screen which bracket the numbers actually came from - it never labels the whole pool 'top 1%'. A feed built before brackets existed serves heroes-{time}.json, and that is tried last, so this file works against an old server too. What each bracket means is written inside every file (the 'mmr' block: bucket, minRating, games) - see server/README.md.
_comment_duo: The same four tables built from DUOS games only - this is what --duo reads. Separate on purpose: a duos lobby is four teams finishing 1st-4th, a solo lobby is eight players finishing 1st-8th, on a different hero pool, so one pooled average would describe neither. There is deliberately no fallback from duos to solo: leave these keys out and --duo shows no numbers rather than the wrong game's numbers.
